relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: While studying at Tokyo University Suzuki took up Zen practice at Engaku-ji, one of Kamakura's Five Mountains, first studying with Imakita Kosen Rōshi.

relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: After Kosen's 1892 passing, Suzuki continued with Kosen's successor at Engaku-ji, Soyen Shaku.

relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: Suzuki lived at Carus's home, the Hegeler Carus Mansion, and worked with him, initially in translating the classic Tao Te Ching from ancient Chinese.

relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: In 1909, Suzuki became an assistant professor at Gakushuin University and at the Tokyo University.

relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: delivered a paper at the World Congress of Faiths in 1936, at the University of London (he was an exchange professor during this year).

relations.subject: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
relations.evidence: From 1952 to 1957 he was a frequent lecturer at Columbia, at one point rising to the position of adjunct professor.
